option_1_bitsandbytes_cpu.reason: BitsAndBytes 4-bit NF4 kernels are compiled strictly for Nvidia CUDA GPUs and are unsupported on CPU on Windows.

option_2_pytorch_native_cpu.reason: Requires minimum 3.2 GB to 5.0 GB free RAM. Host currently has only ~1.25 GB free RAM, causing OS thrashing or MemoryError.

option_3_gguf_llamacpp_conversion.reason: LoRA Checkpoint-200 requires merging with Qwen2.5-1.5B base weights prior to GGUF quantization. The merge operation requires ~4 to 6 GB RAM during weight calculation, exceeding available laptop headroom. Furthermore, converting to Q4_K_M GGUF alters numerical precision and risks accuracy regression on specialized attack tokens.

option_4_remote_gpu_inference.reason: Preserves 100% exact 4-bit NF4 weights and accuracy on Kaggle Tesla T4 (1,692 MB VRAM). Allows the 8 GB Windows laptop to operate smoothly with only 15 MB local RAM overhead.

option_5_deterministic_mock.reason: Optimal for offline test suites and local debugging without internet or GPU.

architectural_recommendation: For an 8 GB Windows laptop without CUDA, the authenticated Remote GPU Inference Server is the optimal, production-grade architecture. It delivers sub-second inference (368 ms/sample) with zero accuracy loss and preserves $> 6$ GB of physical RAM for ordinary Windows applications.
